subtopic: Front-End and Contingent Deferred Sales Loads
source_evidence:
Class A shares might have a front-end sales load paid as a percentage of the purchase price
Class C shares might have a 12b-1 fee and a contingent deferred sales load (CDSL) (a percentage-based fee that investors pay only when they redeem fund shares) for some period of time (often a year).
answer: A front-end sales load is a sales charge paid when you purchase shares, calculated as a percentage of the purchase price. A contingent deferred sales load (CDSL) is a percentage-based charge paid only when you redeem shares; it may apply for a limited period, often a year. These charges work at different points in time, and whether they apply depends on the share class and its terms.
